name: Hispano-Moresque lustreware
summary: Spanish tin-glazed earthenware with a gold-copper lustre, made first by Muslim potters and later by Christian ones. Heraldic shields, plant scrolls and cobalt blue cover large dishes and tall jars.

philosophy.core_thesis: A plain earthenware dish can serve a king when a white glaze, a gold lustre and a heraldic crest cover it in one dense pattern.
design_principles: Dip the earthenware in a white tin glaze and fire it at about 1000 °C.
Paint cobalt blue on the glaze first, for the outlines and the large forms.
Paint the lustre pigment over the glaze and fire a second time in smoke at 600 to 700 °C.
Fill the whole dish with scrolls, ivy, bryony leaves and a central emblem or a coat of arms.
Use radial bands that turn from the centre to the rim, and a raised boss at the centre.
Add a small raised relief to the rim or the cavetto, for the finest large dishes.
Keep the pattern dense and flat, with fine dots and hatching as background.
anti_patterns: A plain white surface with no lustre
A porcelain body that glows with transparency
A thin colourless glaze that shows the buff clay
Bright multicolour enamels in many hues

form.shape: Large circular dishes, deep bowls, albarelli, jugs and tall winged vases (Alhambra vases).
form.profile: A dish has a flat well, a rounded cavetto and a wide rim; a vase has a swelling body and a tall neck.
form.foot_and_rim: A low foot ring with a hole for a hanging cord; a wide, flat rim of 3 to 5 cm.
form.proportion: Dish diameter 35 to 50 cm and a wall 6 to 10 mm thick; a vase up to 1.3 m high.
rules: Pierce the foot ring for a cord, as the dish hangs on a wall.
Divide the dish into a centre emblem and one to three rings.
Keep the rim wide, to carry the scrolls or an inscription.
Place any relief at the centre or the rim, not across the field.

bodies.rule: Use a pale pink to buff earthenware that fires hard enough to carry a thick tin glaze. Keep the body free from fine grey or translucent clays.

forming.joins: Large vases are thrown in sections and joined at the neck and the foot; handles are pulled and luted with slip.
forming.details: Three stilt marks inside the dish, a small hole in the foot ring, and a copper-gold sheen that goes pink or green at an angle.

glaze.pattern: Ivy and bryony scrolls, coats of arms, Arabic-like script and radial bands, in lustre with fine blue outlines.
glaze.gloss: Glossy tin glaze, about 65 to 80 GU, with a metallic lustre.
glaze.wear: The lustre fades or flakes at the rim; the glaze may craze, and the lustre stays bright in sheltered parts.

palette.strategy: A white glaze, a gold-copper lustre and a deep cobalt blue, with a green or a red lustre as a rare variant.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired updraught kiln for the glaze and a smaller, smoky muffle kiln for the lustre firing.
processes: second firing in smoke at 600 to 700 °C
firing.scale: In the 15th century about 20 workshops at Manises sold dishes to the courts of Spain, Italy and France.
firing.signs: A metallic sheen with a brown or green shift, a stilt mark inside the dish and a cord hole in the foot.

pieces.form: Large dish with a coat of arms in the centre and an ivy scroll round the rim
Winged vase of the Alhambra type with a tall neck and gold and blue bands
Albarello-shaped jar with a thin waist and leaf bands
Deep bowl with a raised centre boss and radial relief ribs

positive: gold-copper lustre on white tin glaze
coat of arms in the centre

canonical_works.work: Dish with the arms of Aragon

evidence.title: Vase with scalloped handles, Spain, 14th century

emotion.target_response: A dense, warm splendour: the viewer sees a gold-lit dish covered with pattern and feels courtly wealth in clay.

use_cases: a large wall dish with heraldic pattern
a museum label on Spanish medieval ceramics
a prompt for a gold and blue dish in a castle interior
avoid_when: the brief needs a plain or minimal surface
the brief needs a thin porcelain body

modifiers.how: Remove the heraldic crest and the blue, simplify the pattern to bands and birds, and keep the lustre.
Replace the lustre pattern with polychrome painting of a story in the well of the dish.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Spanish lustreware
